transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-11-18
Time: 16:00 PST
Duration: ~45 mins
Attendees: Sofia (Redwood AE), Devon (Redwood SE), Aisha (Infra), Tom (ML), Maya (Security), Evan (SRE)

Summary: quick sync, network noise still causing intermittent failures; some perf wins after tuning cache but need runtime upgrade and NAT tweak; security asks for KMS policy examples and SOC2 cert copy.

[00:00] Sofia: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh this is our weekly check-in for the private VPC pilot, quick roll call?
[00:08] Aisha: hey, Aisha here
[00:10] Tom: Tom, ML team
[00:12] Maya: Maya, security
[00:13] Evan: Evan SRE
[00:15] Devon: Devon from Redwood, thanks
[00:18] Sofia: cool, agenda is network updates, perf runs and tuning, runtime upgrade plan, security asks, then next steps.

[02:05] Devon: quick status from our side: we ran the KV cache adjustments you asked for, lowered ttl on prefixes and increased cache size for long-lived sessions; saw about 8-12% improvement in token/sec on the 4k context test runs, p95 latency roughly unchanged at first pass.
[02:25] Tom: mmh, yeah we saw that locally too, but we still get weird timeouts during parallel streams, looks like a connection reset from the NAT.
[02:37] Evan: yeah on our side flow logs show spikes where the connections are briefly dropped, typically around scaling events in the target ASG, looks like ephemeral port exhaustion or NAT gateway health flips.
[02:51] Aisha: we did a quick count, NAT ephemeral port usage peaked when all 20 parallel clients started, we have a small pool.

[03:20] Sofia: ok so likely two things: either increase NAT capacity or move to a managed egress setup with a few elastic IPs and preserve mappings; Devon, what did you recommend?
[03:33] Devon: for prod we'd recommend either a NAT gateway autoscale pattern or use VPC egress with NAT instances sized for high ephemeral counts. Also we can do connection pooling at the runtime to reuse sockets — we've got a patch that keeps-alive more aggressively. That helped some customers.
[03:50] Tom: when you say connection pooling at runtime, is that compatible with our tight tenant isolation? We can't have cross-tenant socket reuse.
[03:58] Devon: yes, we keep it per-tenant namespace, it just reuses connections for the same tenant to the Redwood Private runtime; shouldn't cross boundaries. The patch is in our staging branch.

[05:10] Maya: security question — KMS integration: will Redwood call our KMS directly from the private runtime or is it proxied through Redwood control plane? We need to know for our key policies.
[05:23] Sofia: good question. For the private offering the recommended pattern is customer-managed KMS with the runtime calling KMS in your account. The control plane doesn't see plaintext keys. We have a template policy we can share.
[05:34] Maya: ok please send that. Also we need SOC2 docs.
[05:37] Sofia: yes we'll drop SOC2 attestation and PCI/SOC doc links in the follow-up.

[07:00] Devon: on runtime upgrades — we're proposing moving you to runtime 2.1.4 this week; it has improved attention kernels and a fix for socket handling that should reduce the reset events. It also ships CUDA 12.1 and cuDNN 9 compatibility which matches your new node image.
[07:20] Evan: any risk to model outputs during the upgrade? We run a small regression test set but want to avoid drift.
[07:29] Devon: we've validated the kernels against our regression suite; models should be deterministic for same weights, but quantization paths can vary slightly. We'll do a canary on staging first and run the prompt-set diff check.

[09:02] Tom: for the perf numbers — after the cache tweak we saw token/sec go from ~12k to 13.1k on 4k context. Can we get similar gain on 8k?
[09:14] Devon: initial 8k runs showed 10-11% uplift but we haven't done extended runs. We'll run an 8k 1-hour long test to capture steady-state.
[09:23] Sofia: can we schedule that tonight?
[09:26] Devon: I can kick it off after the call, will push logs to the shared S3 link and annotate failures.

[11:00] Aisha: about routing — we plan to test a route table change in staging Tue 11/24 02:00-04:00 UTC. That will pin NAT and disable one ASG scaling policy briefly. Means low-impact window but will simulate the production spike.
[11:16] Sofia: that's fine, Redwood SE will monitor. Please send the exact route table id and we will validate.

[12:20] Tom: small note, during baseline runs we noticed memory growth on long sessions; is that expected with the new KV cache sizes?
[12:31] Devon: might be—if sessions keep large KV stores we do evict but the GC windows in python-java runtimes sometimes lag. We'll instrument and collect heap/alloc profiles for the 1-hour test.

[14:00] Maya: on audit logs, we need at least 12 months retention and full request/response id correlations for compliance. Can you confirm logging granularity?
[14:10] Sofia: Redwood Private can be configured to ship audit logs to your S3 or Splunk; we capture request IDs, model version, route, and metadata. We'll share the log schema. Retention is customer-configurable.
[14:27] Maya: perfect. Also, any objections on network ACLs? We saw a few blocked ephemeral ports but no deliberate policies.
[14:35] Evan: we've allowed ephemeral range 32768-61000 but NAT mapping still limited. Increasing NAT capacity should fix it.

[16:00] Sofia: OK let's recap action items and owners. Devon will run the 8k extended perf test and upload logs by 11/24. Aisha will share VPC flow logs and traceroutes by 11/20. Maya will confirm KMS policy and review SOC2 docs by 11/22. I will send the updated network diagram and NAT recommendations by 11/19.
[16:20] Tom: also please share the runtime upgrade plan and canary checklist.
[16:24] Devon: will include the canary checklist and the regression prompt-set diff results.

[17:00] Sofia: any other blockers?
[17:02] Aisha: none from infra besides the NAT change window.
[17:04] Tom: no
[17:05] Maya: none
[17:07] Sofia: great thanks everyone, we'll follow up by email with links and timeline.
